headline: Isotretinoin
and men.
dek: What the studies of isotretinoin show on mood, sex, sperm and relapse, and what is still unknown.

body: [[/isotretinoin|Isotretinoin]] is the acne pill held back for severe acne that other treatment has not cleared, and for many men the questions go beyond acne, to mood, sex and fertility. Each has a research record of its own, and the findings are mixed.

The Absorica label covers severe recalcitrant nodular acne in non-pregnant patients 12 and older whose acne has not responded to other treatment, including antibiotics.[^label] The approval rests on a double-blind trial that randomized 925 people aged 12 to 54, 60% of them male, to Absorica or another isotretinoin capsule for 20 weeks.[^label] Each started with at least 10 nodules. By week 20, 70% of the Absorica group and 75% of the comparison group had at least a 90% drop in nodule count.[^label] The label adds that a 15 to 20 week course “has been shown to result in complete and prolonged remission of acne in many patients.”[^label]

Not in every patient. In a 2025 JAMA Dermatology cohort study, researchers used US insurance claims to follow 19,907 people for a year or more after a course of at least four months. Of these, 22.5% had a relapse of acne and 8.2% took a second course.[^relapse] Women relapsed more often than men, and a higher total dose over the course was linked with a lower relapse rate; the daily dose, at standard total doses, was not.[^relapse] For adult acne, there are fewer studies. A randomized, placebo-controlled trial tested 5 mg a day, a low dose, against placebo for 16 weeks in adults with milder acne.[^lowdose] Lesion counts fell significantly, and the authors reported that adverse effects “were minimal.”[^lowdose] The trial was industry-sponsored and investigator-initiated, and that 5 mg use is off-label.[^lowdose]

On mental health, the label says the drug “may cause depression, psychosis and, rarely, suicidal ideation, suicide attempts, suicide, and aggressive and/or violent behaviors”.[^label] Among patients who reported depression, it notes, “some reported that the depression subsided with discontinuation of treatment and recurred with reinstitution of treatment.”[^label]

The best known study is Swedish. Researchers linked 5,756 people aged 15 to 49, prescribed isotretinoin for severe acne in the 1980s, to hospital and death records through 2001; 128 were admitted for a suicide attempt.[^sundstrom] Attempts ran above the expected rate during and up to six months after treatment, then fell back to the expected rate by three years.[^sundstrom] The study was observational, and the authors wrote: “However, the risk of attempted suicide was already rising before treatment, so an additional risk due to the isotretinoin treatment cannot be established.”[^sundstrom]

Two meta-analyses pooled the wider record. In 2017, a review in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology combined 31 controlled or prospective studies. It found no significant difference in depression scores between isotretinoin and other acne treatments, and depression became less common after treatment; none of the studies was a randomized trial.[^huang] In 2024, a JAMA Dermatology meta-analysis pooled 25 studies with more than 1.6 million participants.[^tan] The one-year absolute risk of each suicide outcome was under 0.5%.[^tan] Users were slightly less likely than nonusers to attempt suicide two to four years after treatment.[^tan] The authors concluded that at a population level users “do not have increased risk of suicide or psychiatric conditions”.[^tan] One finding differed with the share of men: studies with a higher share of male participants reported a higher one-year absolute risk of completed suicide.[^tan]

Sexual side effects that persist are the second concern. The label lists “sexual dysfunction that may continue after discontinuation of treatment (including erectile dysfunction, decreased libido, decreased vaginal lubrication, and vaginal dryness)”,[^label] adding that “it is not always possible to reliably estimate their frequency or establish a causal relationship to drug exposure.”[^label] In 2017 the UK regulator, the MHRA, reported 49 UK reports of erectile or ejaculation problems and 23 of lower libido since 1985, among roughly 30,000 patients treated a year.[^mhra2017] It wrote that “One possible mechanism for this effect may be through a reduction in plasma testosterone levels.”[^mhra2017]

Later studies diverge. An analysis of US adverse event reports from 2004 to 2024 found that erectile dysfunction, with 195 reports, and decreased libido were reported more often with isotretinoin than with other drugs; such reports cannot show cause.[^faers] A 2018 case series drew 300 reports of lasting sexual problems from a public reporting website, after antidepressants, finasteride-type drugs and isotretinoin, including genital numbness and weak orgasm.[^healy] A 2024 scoping review of 46 human studies found that more than half reported a neutral or beneficial effect on sexual function, and concluded there was “very weak evidence supporting a link between isotretinoin and sexual dysfunction.”[^scoping]

On sperm, the studies are small. The label reports that in trials of 66 men, 30 of them taking the drug, there were no significant changes in sperm count or motility, and that in 50 men aged 17 to 32 there were no significant effects on semen volume, count, motility, shape or seminal fructose.[^label] A 2026 meta-analysis pooled six studies in 225 men. In three acne groups, sperm concentration and vitality rose slightly; no study reported impaired fertility.[^sperm] The authors rated the certainty of evidence low to moderate and called for controlled trials.[^sperm]

In 2023, a UK expert group concluded “it was not possible to say that isotretinoin definitely caused many of the short-term or long-term psychiatric and sexual side effects”.[^mhra2023] UK prescribers must now ask about sexual function before treatment and at each follow-up.[^mhra2026]

In the US, the drug is still dispensed only through iPLEDGE, a program built to prevent birth defects.[^qa] FDA approved changes in February 2026 and moved their start to November 15, 2026.[^ipledge] For patients who cannot get pregnant, which includes men, monthly documentation of counseling will no longer be required and the 30-day pickup window ends.[^ipledge]
What is still unknown is how often lasting sexual or mental effects occur, and whether the drug causes them. The male fertility evidence rests on a few hundred men.
